I believe that students should create their own summer projects because this approach allows for greater creativity, a more enjoyable experience, and reduced stress during the summer months.

During the summer, students have the opportunity to develop highly imaginative projects by exploring various topics, such as scientific experiments or personal narratives. For instance, a student might search for exciting science experiments that not only engage them but also captivate their classmates. Additionally, they could focus on significant figures, either well-known personalities or relatives, and elaborate on their reasons for choosing that individual. Students can design innovative projects, showcasing their creativity to the class while explaining their thought processes and the potential benefits of their inventions.

Moreover, students are likely to have more fun when allowed to pursue their own projects. They will feel more enthusiastic about engaging in activities they have conceived, rather than working on a dull assignment dictated by a teacher. When given the freedom to explore their interests, students can generate extraordinary work. This autonomy removes the constraints of strict guidelines, enabling them to explore ideas freely. They can even collaborate with friends on their projects, enhancing the enjoyment of the experience.

Finally, allowing students to choose their projects can lead to decreased stress levels. They can focus on their work without the pressure of striving for perfection or adhering to rigid criteria. By setting their own objectives, students can share their original plans with their peers, inspiring others to embark on similar enjoyable projects in the future.

In summary, these are my reasons for advocating that students should be responsible for designing their own summer projects.

Additionally, some children may lack access to computers or any technology at home. Sometimes they feel the same way too, so they respond with meanness.

You should spend time together and visit places that both of you enjoy. Their attitude might change because they may need someone to talk to or need to go out more. There are people whose personalities are just different, and you have to accept that.

Lastly, people go through a lot in life, and their personalities can start to change. Additionally, you have to ask them how they feel because sometimes they feel depressed or angry about something and need someone to talk to. It’s better to be there for them or help each other.

In conclusion, people say, "Don't judge a book by its cover," because you never know why they behave the way they do. If you don't know them well, still ask if they're okay. It is possible to change their personality and help them become a better person.

Many people believe that first impressions are very challenging to alter. However, I believe that it is possible to change someone's view of another person through getting to know each other better, spending time together, or simply asking how they feel.

When meeting someone for the first time, if you perceive their character to be negative, it can be beneficial to take the time to understand them more deeply. From my own experiences, I often find myself forming an opinion about someone's demeanor, especially in settings like work or school. Initial interactions can lead to quick judgments based on facial expressions or body language, which can result in equally harsh responses from the other person.

To improve mutual understanding, it’s important to engage in activities that you both enjoy and to share experiences. A person's behavior may shift when they feel supported or when they have the opportunity to open up. People have distinct personalities, and sometimes it’s necessary to embrace those differences.

In addition, individuals encounter various challenges throughout their lives, which can greatly impact their personalities. It’s essential to inquire about their feelings, as they may be dealing with sadness or frustration and might just need someone to listen. Being supportive and helping one another can create a more positive environment.

In summary, there is a saying: "Don't judge a book by its cover," which emphasizes that we cannot always understand someone's behavior without knowing their story. Even if you don’t know someone well, reaching out to see if they are okay can make a significant difference. People can change for the better, and fostering understanding can lead to positive transformations in their character.

Do you believe that students could gain from being able to take classes from home?

Schools are designed to be environments where students feel at ease, and there are numerous options available. In my view, homeschooling presents both pros and cons. On the positive side, students can work without interruptions from peers and can complete their tasks more efficiently. In traditional schools, some students may encounter distractions from classmates who are not genuinely interested in their education, causing them to struggle and potentially repeat a grade. The homeschooling experience is different because, year after year, students can retake courses without the fear of judgment that comes from failing. In a traditional setting, repeating a year can feel embarrassing, which is an important factor to consider.

Homeschoolers often receive more individualized attention, as they benefit from a one-on-one learning experience. Although public schools aim to provide similar support, larger classes mean that teachers may not have the ability to reach every student equally. Many children wish to attend conventional schools but may face obstacles such as disabilities or being in the public eye as celebrities. In such cases, students might prefer homeschooling to avoid constant attention, but they may also feel confined at home and long for the opportunity to socialize. Engaging with peers is essential for personal growth.

Another advantage of homeschooling is the potential for a quicker completion of coursework. While numerous resources are available, some amenities are missing, such as free lunch provided by most public schools. These schools offer a comprehensive, no-cost education, whereas homeschooling can be costly since families must supply their own meals and pay for internet and computer access. Despite these expenses, the investment can be worthwhile, as a good education ultimately leads to future opportunities.

There is certainly value in receiving an education from home, especially since it contributes to a student's future, such as earning a diploma. In conclusion, whether one opts for public school, private school, or homeschooling, each educational path has its own advantages that can benefit students in various ways.

A year ago, I believed that studying business was the right path for me, but I found it incredibly challenging. I struggled in the class and ultimately failed, which left me feeling stressed and unsure of my next steps. It dawned on me that business was not the ideal choice for my future, but I initially thought it was too late to make a change. After discussing my concerns with my counselor, she reassured me that I could switch majors. As a result, I opted for a different field, and now I feel certain about my decision. However, I remain uncertain if I might change my mind again, as I can be indecisive. I've come to understand that this is a common experience; discussions with classmates revealed that many of them share similar doubts. While some argue that early commitment to a career is beneficial, allowing students to take relevant courses in high school, I believe it is detrimental for young people to fixate on a career too soon. This is because they may choose a path that is not suitable for them, leading to uncertainty about their future studies.

Some people contend that choosing a career early on is advantageous since it enables students to tailor their high school classes to support their future ambitions. However, they often overlook how this can negatively impact students. Every day, I hear peers expressing their struggles, saying things like, "This class is really difficult for me, but I can’t switch because it’s necessary for my future career." Those remarks reflect their dissatisfaction and stress.

To truly support students, they should have the opportunity to switch careers if needed. It's possible that the initial path they chose isn't right for them, or they may still be trying to figure out what they want to study.

There are numerous reasons why committing to a career at a young age can be problematic, but I'll highlight two key points.

Firstly, it is unwise for students to lock themselves into a career too early because they might end up selecting a field that does not align with their true interests. Children often aspire to replicate their parents’ paths, either studying the same subjects or attending the same universities. In many cases, parental pressure can lead students to pursue careers they do not truly want. This typically results in frustration and unhappiness, as students come to realize that they chose the wrong career. Consequently, they may contemplate leaving school altogether because they believe the workload is overwhelming, unaware that their discontent stems from choosing an unsuitable path. If statistics were gathered on how students feel about their chosen careers, I believe a significant majority would express dissatisfaction.

Secondly, committing to a career at a young age can lead to indecision regarding what students want to study. With a plethora of options available, selecting just one can be overwhelming. Students might discover skills that are beneficial in a different field, even if their abilities suit the profession they originally chose. Sometimes, this leads them to pursue another career entirely. Life revolves around making decisions, and when students realize they’ve made a poor choice in their careers, they are still learning. They may end up exploring multiple paths by taking diverse courses to reach their goals. Experiencing various subjects can help students uncover what truly resonates with them and support their future careers.

In summary, it is not wise for students to commit to a career at a young age because they may choose an inappropriate field and often feel uncertain about their choices. Young people can be impulsive when selecting their career paths, failing to fully grasp what suits them best. Moreover, they might struggle to decide on their direction altogether. The most effective way to assist students is to guide them in discovering their true interests. Ultimately, this will lead to more confident decisions about their studies.

In a group setting, responsibilities can be split among the members, allowing everyone to contribute their strengths to various aspects of the project. Each individual brings unique skills that can assist with parts of the project that may be challenging for others.

Additionally, team collaboration serves as an excellent opportunity for students to cultivate their cooperative skills. This is vital because many businesses assign tasks to groups rather than individuals, allowing team members to leverage their diverse knowledge. Companies commonly promote the idea of "working as a team" to enhance their overall efficiency. Educators should recognize this as a valuable method for providing students with experiences in teamwork, which ultimately enriches our learning.

Moreover, when teachers permit group work, they help students build confidence. Engaging in discussions with peers about project topics enables students to explore various approaches to tackling challenges. Schools also offer after-school hours, which can accommodate students who may not have a chance to meet at someone's home. Group work can be particularly beneficial for those struggling to meet deadlines since they can rely on their teammates for support, thus improving their overall productivity.

In conclusion, no student should face the burden of handling a large project alone without the chance to collaborate with others. Many companies recognize the efficiency of teamwork and assign tasks to multiple individuals accordingly. Similarly, educators should adopt this approach in their classrooms to aid students in achieving better grades and being more productive in submitting their work. Allowing group work can enhance students’ cooperation skills and expose them to diverse perspectives, leading to better outcomes in their studies.

When was the last occasion you paused from scrolling through your phone to appreciate the beauty of the sky? The first action most people take upon waking is to check their phones. We rely on technology in our daily lives; it has become an integral part of existence. While technology continues to progress and develop, the question arises: are we keeping pace? We often invest our lives in the digital realm, measuring our worth against others. It’s no surprise that many are feeling down; they focus on what others possess, often overlooking the importance of their own accomplishments. Although everyone views the same content, their interpretations can vastly differ.

A major issue is the amount of time wasted. People’s eyes remain fixated on their personal screens. Like sheep, they are absorbed by what’s trending—what's new, what's desirable, what's unfavorable. Their primary concern revolves around their phones and the latest fashion items emblazoned with logos like "Supreme." They vie for the most likes and the greatest social media recognition, prioritizing a fabricated existence online. Many engage in negative interactions via screens, shying away from real conversations. They fear not fitting in unless they possess the latest gadgets, the most impressive items, or the priciest products, believing that higher costs equate to greater value. This attachment to technology results in hours spent glued to screens. Consequently, both minds and bodies suffer; slouching and poor posture are widespread among many. Personally, I have experienced back issues due to my own poor posture as a child, and I foresee a future where arched backs are the norm and only those with good posture will stand out. After all, it’s difficult to present oneself confidently if one's back is hunched.

While technology does offer some advantages, such as readily available answers for school assignments or even fostering new relationships and opportunities, the real concern lies in its misuse. It can be a double-edged sword; it aids us while simultaneously causing harm, yet many fail to recognize this delicate balance.

Nevertheless, when faced with failure, it's common for people to feel like giving up. This topic deserves attention as it highlights the importance of resilience and determination against quitting.

The first reason we should embrace persistence is that failure serves as a powerful teacher. When you encounter setbacks, it's crucial to remember that it's not the end. If you stumble or make a mistake, you'll gain insight for future attempts. It's essential to recognize that your aspirations are achievable through hard work. When you stand firm for your convictions, you pave the way for success.

Many individuals who face difficulties might feel they've wasted their time and choose to surrender. However, life is about facing challenges and embracing the inevitable failures that come our way. While these moments are uncomfortable, we must keep striving forward, aiming for success and the satisfaction that arises from not giving up.

Conversely, those who decide to quit ultimately face failure. Individuals who assume they can effortlessly secure a job, gain admission to a prestigious school, or follow their dreams without encountering any obstacles are often the first to throw in the towel when things get tough. In contrast, those who land significant positions or get accepted to esteemed institutions have typically put in substantial effort. Even in adverse situations, they remain committed to their goals. People who fail often feel inadequate and question their intelligence. If you believe you lack intelligence, consider how you've arrived at this point. When facing difficulties, remember that friends and family can be your greatest allies, helping you navigate through tough times.

In conclusion, whenever you set an objective or aspire to achieve something meaningful, it is crucial to stay committed and not abandon your efforts halfway. Goals represent what you strive to attain, and with perseverance, you can reach them sooner than you think. If you encounter obstacles or experience setbacks, the support of your close ones will help guide you. By refusing to give up on your pursuits, you can foster self-confidence and carry that assurance throughout your life.

School plays a crucial role in an individual's life; however, it consumes a significant portion of both students' and teachers' days. In a typical public middle school in Maryland, classes begin at 8:15 AM and conclude at 3:00 PM. This results in a lengthy school day of 7 hours and 25 minutes, during which students are bombarded with information without pause. Therefore, the school board should refrain from extending the school day, as doing so would reduce the time students need for essential future activities, such as completing homework, engaging in after-school programs like sports, and participating in community service.

Students would find themselves with reduced time for homework or studying. They already invest more than seven hours in school, usually attending 6 to 8 classes that last about 45 minutes each. Out of these classes, at least three often assign homework, meaning students need adequate time to complete their assignments thoroughly. If school hours were lengthened, students would struggle to find enough time for their homework, potentially leading to lower grades due to missed assignments.

Additionally, extending the school day would limit students' opportunities to engage in after-school activities such as sports and clubs. Regular physical activity is crucial for everyone, and since not all students have physical education (P.E.) as part of their curriculum, they might not receive the necessary exercise each day. Even for those who do participate in P.E., the typical class is only 45 minutes long, which may not suffice for a healthy lifestyle. If the school day were to be lengthened by an hour and a half, students would likely have less time for practice with their sports teams. Clubs, which offer valuable experiences and learning opportunities outside of the regular school hours, would also see reduced time for participation, negatively affecting those involved.

Furthermore, students would have diminished opportunities to volunteer in community service projects. Many academic programs require a certain number of community service hours. From my own experiences, I've needed to complete 75 hours through various volunteer tasks, such as assisting teachers or organizing classrooms, typically conducted after school and taking about two hours. If the school day were extended, students would struggle to fulfill their community service requirements, risking failure due to insufficient volunteering hours.

In conclusion, it is more practical for the school board to avoid adding extra hours to the school day. This would allow students to better balance their current responsibilities while still engaging in vital extracurricular activities, such as sports, clubs, and community service.

Many individuals believe that altering first impressions is quite challenging. Our experiences shape how we present ourselves, and our behavior, choice of words, and physical appearance reveal our true selves. This view is widely accepted since while one can modify their looks and communication, the initial impressions tend to stick.

To begin with, the way you conduct yourself during a first meeting is crucial. The saying “actions speak louder than words” holds a lot of truth. Your behavior is often the most telling aspect of your first impression. When you interact with someone new, it is important to avoid being unkind or disrespectful. If you act negatively, people might conclude that you are not the right person to be around. Therefore, it is essential to make a positive impact from the very start.

Moreover, when conversing with someone for the first time, it’s wise to refrain from using inappropriate language. Using offensive words could lead them to think you lack basic conversational skills. You can choose to speak plainly or use more complex vocabulary. Regardless of how often you communicate well, each interaction helps build their trust in you. It’s also important to strive for clarity in your speech and try not to stammer excessively, as frequent mistakes can affect how you’re perceived. Many are understanding and may offer a second chance even if you stumble. Additionally, it’s advisable to keep your hands still during initial introductions to maintain a composed demeanor.

Furthermore, your appearance plays a significant role in forming first impressions. Unlike behaviors or words, your external look reflects who you are and is largely unchangeable at the moment of meeting someone. People tend to focus on appearances when making judgments. If you present yourself poorly, others might view you negatively and choose not to engage. Conversely, a well-groomed appearance can attract potential friendships, contingent upon their own initial perceptions.

If others find your actions or speech appealing, as well as your appearance, they might want to connect. Positive first impressions can be hard to shake off, and changing them afterward is not an easy task.

However, it is also possible to alter people's perceptions over time. Everyone has ups and downs; a bad day can influence your interactions. Some individuals will recognize that you're not typically like that during tough times. Regardless of the circumstances, there remains an opportunity for second chances regarding first impressions.

In conclusion, while many believe that first impressions are unchangeable, they are a crucial aspect of human interaction. Key elements such as actions, words, and appearance shape these impressions. People continually learn from their experiences. Therefore, it is vital to be mindful of how you act, speak, and present yourself to others, as we encounter new people every day.

For those with jobs, this structure would allow them to work and earn necessary money without conflicting with their education. Students burdened with substantial homework would have the extra day to stay on top of their assignments, ensuring that all their work is done. Furthermore, this extra day could also provide opportunities for engaging in sports or other leisure activities.

By reducing the school week to four days, significant energy savings would be achieved. Many of our natural resources are not renewable, so it is essential to take steps to conserve water, electricity, and other resources. A shorter school week would contribute to substantial energy savings, particularly since the costs associated with electricity for large buildings like schools can be quite high.

For these reasons, schools should consider adopting a four-day schedule to reduce costs and conserve energy, ensuring that educational institutions are well-equipped for the future.

Having someone to confide in can be invaluable. Being part of a school allows students to connect with hundreds of peers and form friendships. Reflecting on her mother’s insights, Generic_Name decided that attending regular classes was the better choice. Enrolling in traditional education means students can avoid feelings of loneliness and have the chance to build social connections.

Another point in favor of traditional schools is the availability of clubs and extracurricular activities. Online learning lacks the social engagement and opportunities for participation found in in-person education. Public schools provide a wide range of clubs and activities that students can enjoy, which are crucial for their development. Such activities not only help students discover their interests but also prepare them for future careers. For example, a student who loves football could join the football team, paving the way for potential scholarships or opportunities in larger leagues. Participating in clubs enables students to explore future career paths, gain new experiences, and develop their skills through various activities.

After-school activities are excellent for keeping young people engaged and steering them toward positive paths in life. Schools offer a diverse range of ways to learn and have fun, blending education with enjoyment.

Online Learning

Who doesn't want to be left in the house all day using an electronic device with online access? Although students save money and time by taking classes from home. It is not beneficial to learn online because students lose focus of what they are learning and tend to easily get distracted when they're in their house, students can't have a one on one conversation with a teacher nor discuss with classmates, and students could also face technical difficulties when attending online classes from home.

Losing focus has a big impact in learning. For example, my friend Generic_Name sent me a text message last month, right when I started studying for my history mid-term exam. I responded back to Generic_Name's text, and without realizing we kept on messaging past midnight. This shows how easily students get distracted at home with a cellular device and how easy it is to lose focus. The next morning I decided to get to school an hour early and review one on one with my teacher.

Secondly, taking classes online doesn't just mean you don't have a physical teacher or instructor that you can question lively, but also means that it will be challenging to find answers to your questions. I remember in my sophomore year a kid in our econ class named Generic_Name was really sick for a while so he had ended up taking classes online. Generic_Name was a straight A student, always was first to answer the teachers questions and he also used to ask questions. Thankfully Generic_Name healed towards the end of the year and I asked him if he benefited and if he recommends attending classes from home. The straight A student Generic_Name said it was a real challenge to take the class online and he finished the class a month after he should have with a B- average. Generic_Name had also said that one of the most difficult parts about attending a class online was his laptop not functioning at all times, and not having a teacher you can talk and converse with one on one.

Finally, using your personal computer and internet connection can always be an issue. You can't always depend on your computer, not just the computers but even people aren't perfect. Another main problem Generic_Name had when attending classes online was his laptop and network connection. Generic_Name explained that he always faced technical difficulties. When his laptop wasn't functioning right, the only thing he could do was to stop the lesson and wait for his dad to get the laptop repaired, which took time. Each month, either his laptop or internet connection would not cooperate, so he finished the class a month later than everyone.

In conclusion, Everyone would like to save money and time by taking classes from home. But getting distracted, not asking your teacher questions when you need to, and wasting money on laptop repair is not worth it at all. Learning from a far distance could also be an option but when asking if it is beneficial, we can say that it is not by looking at the listed reasoning.

After ascending there and failing to find the store, she seeks assistance again. This time, another individual informs her that the store is actually on the first floor beside the ice cream parlor. Generic_Name then makes her way down, grabs an ice cream, and finally finds her desired store. She felt immense relief at having located it, realizing that without the second opinion, she might have left empty-handed.

Moreover, having multiple perspectives is advantageous in other situations as well. Imagine Generic_Name moved to New York for her first day of high school and was unsure of how to reach her school, and her parents were also at a loss. They instructed her to follow the school-aged kids she spotted. She approached a girl with blue eyes and brown hair, thinking, “She looks like she knows where to go.” Introducing herself, she learned they were both in high school. However, once at the school, they parted ways, and Generic_Name found herself confused and lost. As she wandered the hallways, she began asking various students for directions, receiving consistent answers pointing her to the same place. This highlights the importance of seeking multiple opinions; if she had relied on only one source, she could have ended up in the wrong classroom.

Finally, another significant benefit of seeking various opinions is problem-solving capability. Take the case where Generic_Name invites two friends over for a sleepover. While enjoying their time in the kitchen, her mother warns them against cooking. Suddenly, a fire breaks out in the oven. In a panic, Generic_Name exclaims, “What should I do?” One friend suggests calling 911, while the other dismissively recommends throwing water on it, claiming it will be fine. Ultimately, Generic_Name opts to call 911, recognizing it as the wiser choice. The emergency services arrive promptly and resolve the crisis.

In conclusion, seeking multiple opinions can significantly enhance decision-making by providing diverse perspectives, increasing the number of options available, and aiding in problem resolution. Generic_Name successfully navigated her way through finding the right store, locating her school, and preventing a disaster at home. It’s clear that serious issues could have arisen had she not sought multiple viewpoints.

Should schools regulate the number of extracurricular activities a student can participate in? It is important to acknowledge that schools should have some level of influence when it comes to managing a student's involvement in out-of-school activities. Ultimately, the student's family should play a crucial role in making decisions about their participation. If a student begins to struggle academically, it is reasonable for parents to request the school to limit their extracurricular commitments, especially if the student is unable to attend meetings regularly. In such cases, the school can step in to help determine the best course of action.

To begin with, I believe there should be some limitations on the number of activities a student can join, although the choice should primarily rest with the student and their family, as they are the key decision-makers. If a family observes that the child is unable to complete homework or prepare for exams due to their commitments, they should engage in a discussion with the student about their concerns and listen to their perspective. If they decide to allow the child to continue with extracurricular activities, that is their prerogative; however, if they opt to withdraw their child from certain activities, it is essential to inform the guidance counselor and the leader of the specific activity.

On the other hand, if a student starts to see a decline in their grades, it is the responsibility of their guidance counselor to speak with them to uncover the reasons for this drop. If it is determined that the student is overloaded with extracurriculars, a conversation should occur to identify which activities could be paused until their academic performance improves. This approach should encourage the student to understand that maintaining good grades is crucial if they wish to remain involved in their preferred activities.

Finally, if a student demonstrates poor attendance at meetings and is frequently absent, they should be barred from participating in extracurricular activities. A student should not miss more than five meetings in a month without facing any repercussions. If a child must be removed from a club, their parents should be informed of the reasons behind this decision. Furthermore, without valid justification, the child may face a temporary suspension from attending future meetings.

In summary, schools should have minimal influence on whether a student can partake in extracurricular activities. The primary authority in this matter should lie with families, unless the student is experiencing academic difficulties or has a pattern of poor meeting attendance. In cases where a student’s grades are slipping or they fail to attend meetings regularly, it may be necessary for the school to intervene.

Some individuals believe that allowing cell phones in classrooms is a negative practice, as students tend to start texting their friends the moment they pick up their devices. Conversely, others argue that cell phones can be a valuable educational tool if used appropriately. I hold the view that permitting cell phones in classrooms will ultimately lead to distractions, reduced attention spans, and incomplete assignments.

Many students tend to browse through social media platforms like Snapchat, Instagram, and Facebook instead of focusing on the lesson. For instance, during a recent group project, one of my teammates was listening to music on his phone while we were supposed to collaborate. When it was our turn to present, he was unprepared and consequently received a failing grade for that assignment.

Another critical reason against cell phone usage in classrooms is that it can hinder students' attentiveness to their teachers. This poses a significant challenge since educators might become frustrated when they notice that students are disengaged. I find that I, too, might lose focus and start watching my favorite shows instead. Only a handful of students may remain attentive, usually due to pressure from their parents. Without that motivation, I truly believe that few would listen to their teachers, and not paying attention during instructions could lead to poor academic performance.

Lastly, schools should consider prohibiting cell phones to ensure that students complete their work. Knowing that I can easily access my phone often makes me lazy and less inclined to do my assignments. Failing to complete homework and class activities can ultimately result in poor grades and have lasting consequences post-graduation. I have my own experience to share; during my junior year, I was using my phone in chemistry class while we were conducting a lab experiment. I accidentally spilled some chemicals on my phone, rendering it unusable. When I shared this incident with my parents, they were not pleased. They reminded me of the irresponsibility of using my phone during critical tasks, linking this to my declining grades.

In conclusion, permitting cell phones in classrooms is not a wise decision, as many students tend to neglect their responsibilities. Their dependency on these devices prevents them from engaging with their work. The distraction of cell phones does not contribute positively to learning; instead, focusing on assignments and listening to teachers fosters smart and responsible individuals. Education is vital to achieving success, and neglecting that opportunity can diminish our efforts towards growth.

Most students look forward to enjoying their summer vacation. For many, this time off is a chance to escape from school worries. However, some students prefer to shorten summer break in favor of having longer vacations during the winter, spring, and fall. While there are valid points on both sides of this debate, I believe that a lengthy summer vacation is more beneficial, accompanied by shorter breaks in winter and spring. My main arguments revolve around the difficulty of making long-term plans during a short vacation and the effectiveness of longer periods of continuous school.

One key reason for my stance is that shorter vacations make it challenging for students to create long-term plans. Many students yearn to travel or explore new countries, but when breaks are brief, they often find themselves preoccupied with schoolwork and assignments during their trips. It can be frustrating to not have enough time to see everything one wishes to, leading to feelings of regret for not having had more time. If a student has family residing abroad, they naturally wish to maximize their time together during breaks, especially if visits are infrequent. They want to cherish those moments because the next reunion could be uncertain, ranging from a year to a decade away. Unfortunately, if students have to cut their visit short, they won’t fully enjoy their time with loved ones. Thus, I strongly support extended summer vacations.

Another significant reason backs my opinion: it is inefficient to have a short school term followed by a break. Just like athletes who focus intensely during their competitive seasons without long interruptions, students also benefit from maintaining a rhythm in their studies. For instance, musicians aiming to excel must practice consistently. Aiming for ten hours of practice one day and doing nothing for a week won’t yield progress. Regular daily practice, even for shorter periods, reinforces skills and aids improvement. Transitioning back to school after an extended break can be tough, but adapting to a regular routine is easier than restarting after frequent short breaks. This suggests that a long summer vacation is more beneficial.

While there are advantages to the opposing view, as not every student learns the same way, there are risks linked to cramming. Some students thrive on studying intensely for a limited time before taking a break, and while they may perform well on tests, they risk forgetting material over the break as they try to absorb vast amounts of information in a short span. Therefore, although test performance might be temporarily high for those who cram, long-term retention is often compromised. This further strengthens the case for favoring longer summer breaks over shorter ones.

In conclusion, summer vacation represents a highlight of the academic year for students. Almost everyone has plans for how to make the most of this time. Despite the stressors that lead some students to advocate for shorter summer breaks, it is essential to realize that extending winter and fall vacations can jeopardize summer plans. Moreover, they should understand that a longer break provides numerous opportunities. Ultimately, how individuals choose to utilize their time is crucial, but having a more extended vacation period significantly enhances the potential for meaningful experiences.

They say the you should never judge a book by its cover and, especially regarding people, its true. In this case, the cover is not necessary meaning the appearance, but the first impression of another person. Like the cover of a book, first impressions are not always as appealing as what is really there. its not until after you start "reading" or get to know someone, when you really find out that what you see is not always what you get. There are several factors that can affect the first impression that one receives from another. Differing personality, situations and representation of a person, make impressions often the worst means of judging people.

A person's personality has a big effect on the first impressions that they emit. Everybody is different but when it comes down to it first impressions are really based off of whether you are shy or not. I met my best friend after moving during my junior year, at my new high school. Before i knew her, she never said a word to me or anyone else in the classes that she was kind of odd, but then realized that I was the same way, i didn't talk to many people either because of my personality. I knew that I was shy person and after I get to know someone, I put down my front and show my true colors. I thought that maybe she would be same way. After starting to talk to her a little more each day, our friendship grew and I learned that she wasn't odd at all, but just like me an outgoing person hidden by their shyness. Some people like me and my friend, are shy and put up a reserved and quiet front when facing new people. Based on my first impressions of my friend, I thought something that was far from the truth. One who has a shy personality might in reality be outgoing, but uncomfortable showing it at first, making the first impression of that person a mistaken one.

Your first impression of someone is not suitable because you do not know the situation they may be in. When seeing or meeting someone new, you have no idea the kind of day,

difficulties or kind of disappointment that person may be experiencing. They may have have recently lost someone, or could be someone new and yet still have to deal with the routines and stresses going through out their day. All of these situations can create a barrier between themselves and others, and setting of a good impression is probably not at the top of their list of important things to do.

On my first day of senior year, I walked hurriedly to my first class, even thought I had plenty of time to get there. When I walked into my class, the only thing on my mind was to find a seat right away, no matter if it was by another person or not. when the time come to eat lunch, I sat by myself and ate it quickly so I could proceed to my next class. I was so worried about being late for a class, finding a seat and just doing things right, that i didn't have time to try to leave any good first impression, on any of my peers. It wasnt even on my mind to do so. My peers received the impression that i was nervous and not a sociable person, when really I was acting the way I was because of the situation that I was in.

There are many factors that lead to someone's first impression of another. Someone;s personality, current situation, or the way they happen to present themselves all influences the way someone thinks about another when seeing or meeting them for the first time. Since what they think is based off of these judgments, their first impressions is usually wrong. If all friendships were based on first impressions, there would be a lot less of them in the world. It is often said that one should not judge a book by its cover, and this sentiment holds especially true when it comes to people. In this context, the "cover" does not just refer to a person's appearance but rather to the initial impression we form of them. Just like the surface of a book may not reflect its story accurately, first impressions can be misleading, and it is only once we begin to "read" or engage with someone that we discover that what meets the eye is not always the complete truth. Numerous factors can influence the first impression we receive from someone, such as their personality, current circumstances, and how they present themselves, making these initial judgments often the least reliable way to assess a person.

A person's personality plays a significant role in shaping the first impressions they convey. While everyone is unique, initial perceptions are frequently based on whether an individual is outgoing or reserved. For instance, I met my closest friend during my junior year after moving to a new high school. Initially, she did not speak to me or anyone else, and I found her to be a bit unusual. However, I soon realized I was quite similar; I, too, struggled to engage with others due to my shy nature. I understood that, like me, she might just be hesitant to express herself at first. As our conversation progressed over several days, I discovered that she was not odd but simply another outgoing person who was masked by her shyness. Individuals like my friend and I may create a quiet and reserved facade when encountering new people. My first impression of her turned out to be quite inaccurate. Someone who appears shy can actually be vibrant and outgoing once they feel comfortable, leading to an erroneous initial impression.

Another reason why first impressions can be misleading is that we often fail to consider the circumstances someone is facing at the moment we meet them. When we encounter someone for the first time, we are unaware of the challenges, disappointments, or stressors they might be dealing with. They could be coping with a recent loss or grappling with the strains of adjusting to a new environment. In such contexts, presenting oneself well may not be their priority, as they might be overwhelmed with personal issues.

Reflecting on my own experiences, I remember my first day of senior year, where I hastily rushed to my first class, even though I had ample time. My only focus was finding a seat quickly, regardless of whom I sat next to. At lunch, I ended up eating alone, hurriedly finishing my meal so I could make it to my next class. I was so preoccupied with the idea of being on time and ensuring everything went smoothly that I didn't spare a thought for making a positive first impression on my classmates. As a result, my peers perceived me as anxious and unfriendly, while in reality, my behavior was shaped entirely by my situation.

Overall, many factors contribute to the first impression one person forms of another. The interplay of personality, immediate circumstances, and the way someone showcases themselves all affect how we think about each other upon first meeting. As these perceptions are often based on fleeting judgments, first impressions can frequently be incorrect. If all relationships were reliant on these initial encounters, we would likely see far fewer friendships flourishing. First impressions are typically the least effective way to evaluate someone; it is through getting to know a person better that we can truly understand their character and appreciate the individual for their genuine qualities, rather than merely their initial appearance or "book cover."

Technology has both positive and negative aspects, with some innovations proving beneficial and others potentially harmful and destructive. The question arises: has technology become essential in our daily routines, or have we grown too reliant on it, becoming lazy in performing tasks ourselves? I believe that the diminishing of face-to-face interactions due to technology has resulted in numerous adverse effects on individuals. This reliance can lead to feelings of isolation or depression, cause some individuals to lose their grasp on reality, and negatively impact both physical and mental health. In the same vein, technology can lead to various harmful consequences.

To elaborate, the connection between technology and depression or isolation can create dire situations, especially when both conditions are present. The rise of social media has facilitated bullying, particularly among young people, severely affecting their emotional well-being. Consequently, some children may choose to withdraw from social situations, avoiding school and friends. Many individuals become so immersed in video games that they fail to realize they are distancing themselves from their immediate surroundings. With the prevalence of mobile devices, it is common for people to spend their days glued to their screens, neglecting real-life interactions. Technology’s influence on mental health is profound, often leading to depressive symptoms.

Furthermore, technology can sever people's connection to reality. The internet makes it easy for individuals to be manipulated. Young children are particularly susceptible to this, as they often consume content from television and platforms like YouTube. Many such videos can lead children to believe in falsehoods or even indoctrinate them with misleading ideas. Adults are not immune either, as they can also be easily misled by information found online. The internet is rife with conspiracy theories suggesting that technological advancements are part of brainwashing efforts, and some people accept these claims without question. Moreover, excessive gaming can cause young individuals to blur the lines between virtual actions and real-life consequences.

As technology continues to evolve, it is likely to exacerbate issues related to physical and mental health. Eye care professionals warn that prolonged screen time can harm vision. Moreover, technology can alter individuals’ personalities, as some may imitate their online idols, changing their appearance and behavior. Additionally, many are drawn to risky challenges showcased online, often leading to serious injuries that result in hospital visits.

On the flip side, technology does offer significant advantages. It can save lives in emergencies and provide vital assistance in military endeavors. Technological advancements enhance efficiency in numerous aspects of our lives, simplifying tasks and alleviating some stress. While technological progress has the potential to revolutionize our existence, it is essential to recognize its risks. Technology can fail unexpectedly, and in some cases, it can even be dangerous. It may seem that technology simplifies life, but excessive dependence could lead to more challenges. If individuals allow machines to carry out all tasks for them, their physical well-being is likely to deteriorate due to a lack of necessary exercise. Furthermore, it is crucial to acknowledge that technology is disrupting the beauty of our planet. Its contributions to pollution are detrimental to our environment.

In conclusion, technology is contributing to various issues that often go unnoticed until we assess our surroundings. I firmly believe that the reduction of human contact in favor of technology leads to negative outcomes, as it can disconnect people from the outside world, provoke depression or isolation, and have harmful effects on physical and mental health. While technology can be downplayed, it is unlikely to disappear from our lives entirely.

During my high school years, I encountered a teacher who appeared quite unfriendly and seemed reluctant to engage with students or repeat explanations of the material he covered. Faced with this situation, I approached my counselor to discuss the possibility of switching classes, but she informed me that it wasn't an option. However, after spending some time in his class, I discovered that he was not only an excellent educator, but also a kind individual. Whenever I sought his assistance, he consistently made an effort to help me grasp the subject matter and perform well on tests and quizzes. It is often said that first impressions are difficult to alter, leading many to believe that one can accurately assess a person's character based solely on initial encounters. However, I argue that first impressions can indeed be misleading, as they may stem from a person's bad day, highlighting the importance of understanding someone's true character before forming judgments.

Around the globe, everyone has off days, and this is a natural aspect of life, which is a mix of ups and downs. On days when someone is feeling low, their attitude towards others may understandably suffer. Many factors, such as difficulties at home, work, or school, can impact how an individual behaves, and this can result in either friendly or unfriendly interactions. When first encountering someone who seems unpleasant, it doesn't necessarily indicate that they have a negative personality; it could simply mean they are experiencing a tough moment. To accurately evaluate someone's character, it is essential to get to know them better first.

In life, it’s unwise to rush to conclusions about others based solely on their actions or outer appearance. A well-known saying, "Don't judge a book by its cover," emphasizes that our assumptions about a person based on their looks don't reflect who they are internally. Some individuals might give off an impression of being kind and considerate, yet ultimately prove to be untrustworthy, leaving you at a loss for having placed your faith in them based on superficial judgments. Conversely, there are those who might appear unapproachable or unfriendly, but in reality, they could possess a warm and helpful nature that you may need to rely on at some point.

In summary, first impressions can change as circumstances may lead individuals to behave poorly on certain days. Moreover, by getting to know someone more deeply, we are likely to reevaluate our initial thoughts about them. It is crucial to understand a person’s true character before passing judgment, as the very individual you reject or criticize at first could turn out to be someone who becomes invaluable in your life later on.

Consequently, some people prefer that students wait until college to make such decisions.

Once they reach college, they must be ready to select a major, and if they are indecisive, they risk choosing a field they are not truly passionate about. This could lead to prolonged college years or even dropping out, ultimately affecting their job prospects and future.

In conclusion, committing to a career at a young age is indeed a wise decision. It provides students with an opportunity to prepare effectively for their futures. School is a place where students have to tackle various assignments, and the choice to complete them lies solely with each individual. The way students handle their work has an impact on how teachers perceive them and can influence their future development. One aspect that I find problematic in education is the tendency of teachers to praise students who do not put forth their best effort. I believe that genuine self-esteem arises from real achievements, and it is misleading to encourage those who aren’t sincerely attempting to improve.

Firstly, I oppose the method some teachers use to boost students' self-confidence because it fosters dependency. When students rely on external validation, they often seek constant support from others. In reality, the world does not offer that kind of safety net. If they become too reliant on praise, they may expect recognition for minimal effort. This could lead to a troubling situation; if they find themselves without any support, they might lack the motivation to accomplish anything at all.

Secondly, such encouragement can prevent students from experiencing genuine success. Achieving a goal brings about a sense of joy and fulfillment. If students continuously receive praise for their attempts, they may never feel compelled to fully complete a task, thinking they have done enough already. This mindset could prove detrimental in the long run, as they may struggle with future assignments, believing they have succeeded when the quality of their work is not satisfactory.

While there are some advantages to teachers providing motivation—like fostering confidence and self-esteem—there is a fine line to tread. Encouragement can certainly help students excel in the future, potentially inspiring them to uplift their peers. However, I feel that teachers should avoid excessive praise, especially for the smallest accomplishments, such as simply writing their names. At times, a firm approach is necessary. Although this might be uncomfortable initially, it can lead to better outcomes in the end.

These are the reasons why I do not support the approach of teachers who excessively motivate students. Learners should develop the ability to work independently and not rely on constant guidance. That said, I am not against teachers providing help; rather, they should concentrate their efforts on those who genuinely need assistance. I hope to see a shift where educators focus their support on students who show a real desire to improve.

Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."

High school the place where we can all do anything we want and just a step before going to college, or at least this is what a lot of middle schoolers think. In high school we take so many classes that are required and those classes are supposed to open up doors and get us closer to our goals. But, classes like arts, music or drama will give us something that we cannot get from others classes. These classes are like a little break, just a whole class to forget about having to write an essay or doing some long math equations and, instead just have fun with friends and enjoy singing, painting and even acting. These classes teach the students how to socialize and communicate with others.

High school is not as easy as some would think, students usually get really stressed because they have to pass their classes, their Sols and start getting prepare for college all at the same time. There is where classes like this can give a little opening to reduce some of that stress. Usually the environment in this classes is always joyful and fun, it is a place where students can learn through socializing and having fun. Classes like this not only give a little time off all the stress and pressure from high classes but also can give lessons to students that they would never even imagined they would learn.

In life being able to express ourselves is something required, something that we have to do if we want to move keep moving up our hill path. In my view, I am mostly against the idea of schools providing distance learning options, which allow students to attend classes from home using online or video conferencing tools. My opposition is not influenced by the fact that I am enrolled in a public high school. I have several reasons for my stance.

Firstly, I believe this approach can negatively impact students' communication abilities. When taking classes online, students are essentially isolated at home, interacting only with their teacher rather than their peers. Although I have never experienced an online class, I cannot imagine that being disconnected from fellow students is beneficial, especially for those who thrive on teamwork and collaboration. Additionally, classmates often have insights or understand concepts differently; they can provide support and clarification. If students are not physically present with one another, this kind of assistance is lost.

Secondly, I contend that online learning also diminishes participation skills. In a traditional school setting, we are engaged in various activities that relate to the subjects we are studying, which greatly enhances memory retention. Being able to ask questions in real-time fosters a better understanding of the material. There are often nuances that can be overlooked when communicating via email or other means. When learning faces challenges, direct interaction with teachers is far more effective than waiting for responses through electronic communication.

Finally, attending classes from home can lead to laziness and increased absenteeism, which ultimately affects academic performance. This is particularly concerning for students who may struggle with maintaining productivity and commitment in their education. Personally, I know I would likely miss classes due to procrastination or unworthy distractions. While some students are dedicated and organized, able to succeed in an online format, that is not the case for everyone.

To summarize, I have valid reasons for my disagreement with online classes. While it's beneficial for schools to provide distance learning for those who can’t physically attend, I personally do not support this trend.

In this essay, we will explore the different challenges associated with working in teams compared to working alone. The focus will be on examining the pros and cons from the perspective of the individual rather than the group as a whole. We will first analyze the dynamics between group work and individual efforts, and then consider the various issues that arise while collaborating within a team. Additionally, we will discuss how these issues can impact the individual, both positively and negatively.

Think back to the last time you had to work on a project. You likely considered multiple approaches to completing it. A crucial decision that comes to mind early on is whether to tackle the task alone or as part of a team. Everyone knows what it’s like to undertake a task individually since that means being solely responsible for its completion. However, it’s essential to understand what defines a group, how it is formed, and the dynamics at play within it.

A group can be described as a collection of individuals who unite to accomplish a specific objective. The formation, structure, and processes of a group, as well as its overall functioning, are integral aspects of group dynamics. This concept is significant in both formal and informal groups across various contexts. Within any organization, groups are a common entity, making the study of group dynamics an important area in understanding organizational behavior.

Delving into group dynamics, it fundamentally addresses the reasons behind why and how groups are established and evolve. Numerous theories have been proposed to explain these phenomena.

While group work offers numerous advantages, it also presents certain drawbacks. One major issue is that individual members often have less autonomy over the task compared to when one person is responsible for its completion. Furthermore, some individuals may dominate discussions and contributions, leaving others feeling less engaged. As a result, the group may reach its objectives, but at the expense of limiting participation from other students. Nevertheless, teams that collaborate effectively can achieve far more than individuals working in isolation. A wider array of skills can be utilized in practical activities, and exchanging and debating ideas is crucial for fostering a deeper comprehension of particular subjects.

Being part of a team allows you to enhance your interpersonal skills, including communication and active listening, as well as team-building skills like leadership and motivating peers. Many of these abilities will serve you well throughout your academic journey and beyond, highlighting their significance.

To fully capitalize on these advantages, it is essential to manage group collaboration efficiently.

Technology has always acted as a compelling and mysterious field for me. Even as a child, I spent countless hours not playing my video-game consoles as intended, but rather meticulously studying every component of the device in an attempt to crack the mystery on how it operated. Despite the fact that I've grown older and many aspects of my life have changed, my passion for technology has not only remained, but undoubtedly grown stronger as well. Therefore, an internship in this field seems vital in feeding and nurturing this passion. Although I have not had previous experience in shadowing, an opportunity to shadow would be fitting due to my previous experience and ever-growing passion in this field.

My experience in the technological field proves fitting for this opportunity to shadow. In school, I am enrolled in the Center for Information Technology at Generic_School. This specialty center provides me with crucial access to exclusive technology-based courses and teachers that help me broaden my vision in the technology field. Classes such as IT Project Management, Programming, and AP Computer Science Principles are all courses that I have been graciously provided with through the center and received exceptional results in. This daily involvement in technology not only increased my knowledge in this field, but also my curiosity on the subject. Outside of school, I am a member of the Technology Student Association, a club dedicated to assisting students nurture their interests through rigorous competitions. Through this club I have been able to surround myself with peers with similar interests and aspirations. This club has also provided me with opportunities to exhibit my knowledge in the technological field through competitions, receiving first place in States in Mass Production, Junior Solar Sprint, and Biotechnology. My involvement and superior results in these events prove to show not only my interest in this field, but my capabilities as well. These experiences transfer directly over to the internship, allowing for a smooth transition without much confusion.

The passion I have for technology undeniably proves me to be fitting for this internship opportunity. A crucial action that proves my strong interest in technology occurred when high school specialty center results were published. I was accepted into the medical, IB, and the information technology centers. Despite the fact that the majority of my close friends chose to enroll into the medical center, I stuck with my passion and enrolled into the Information Technology center. The action of choosing my interest over my close friends of many years displays how much I value technology and wish to pursue it in the future. In addition, my strong passion for technology can be displayed through the utilization of my free time. While other kids may choose to spend this time by indulging themselves into video games, much of my time is spent educating myself on technology. Many enjoyable hours of activities such as reading on the history of computers or watching videos on the future of technology were spent during this time. This use of my limited free time shows that technology, in my mind, is not a merely a class in school, but rather a hobby or an enjoyable subject. This attitude would no doubt have a beneficial effect for the internship.

In conclusion, the heavy interest and years of experience I have in technology proves me to be exceptional candidate for this shadowing opportunity. Although my work experience is limited, my passion and expierence in technology may help me ease into the internship without trouble. The talent I have in technology mixed with the catalyst that is my preexisting passion for this field helps me understand the importance of this internship. Not only will this internship assist in broadening my horizons on technology, but it will also help nurture and grow this passion into something meaningful and of use to the real world. Therefore, I believe this internship is perfect for me.

Some might argue that change is possible for everyone. However, I believe that many individuals are incapable of altering their behavior towards others. My first point concerns attitude: many people won’t modify how you feel about them, nor will they change their conduct towards you. For instance, I sometimes display an unkind attitude towards my sister, Generic_Name. I often raise my voice at her when she needs my help or asks for something, even though she is three years younger than I am.

My second point relates to violence: certain individuals are unable to change their violent tendencies, which can lead to hurting those closest to them. For example, during middle school, I was a generally kind person who did not harm others, but when I cut my hair, some classmates started to tease me. This upset me and caused me to react with aggression towards those who insulted me. While I still show kindness to friends who understand my feelings, I strive to control my anger to avoid conflicts. Another example is my youngest sister, Generic_Name, who can become aggressive when our other sister, Generic_Name, provokes her. She also makes efforts to manage her anger, just as I do.

Finally, my last point pertains to friends: some individuals may attempt to exploit you for financial gain, like wanting money for clothes just for themselves. Additionally, some might pretend to be friendly while speaking ill of you once you leave. I recall a scene from one of my favorite movies where a group of popular girls seems nice to the new girl, but as soon as she walks away, they make unkind remarks about her, ensuring she is oblivious to their cruelty.

In summary, why do some individuals fail to mature? Their immature behavior often prevents them from changing significantly. I agree with Emerson's point, as many people can exhibit childish traits and are unlikely to transform. My three reasons include having a poor attitude, occasional violent reactions, and the tendency of some friends to exploit or criticize you behind your back.

Those who engage in work they are passionate about typically show greater dedication and proficiency.

Forcing young students to determine their career trajectory too soon could lead to complications later, requiring them to start anew in a field they might prefer. Conducting thorough research and taking the time to plan effectively can make a significant difference in aligning students’ futures with their true interests.

It is essential for students to gather the necessary experiences and insights about their future ambitions before committing to a particular career path.

Are vacations a necessity to us and to our success? Why do we need them? While some say that inactivity gives us time to reinvent ourselves. Others believe that it instigates procrastination. Inactivity serves a purpose because it keeps us from giving up and it allows us time for new ideas.

Inactivity serves a purpose because it keeps us from giving up. For example, I was once taking a very long test that lasted around 4 to 5 hours. At first, I was just guessing my way through it because I was very tired and ready to give up. Then, we were given a five minute break so I got up and walked around a bit. After walking for a few minutes, I was energized and ready to finish the test. With my new found energy, I was very content with the test and my score. In fact, students who take mental breaks during long testing periods score 31% higher than the ones who did not take any breaks. In conclusion, inactivity keeps us enthusiastic about our work.

Inactivity serves a purpose because it allows us time for new ideas. For example, one of my friends named Generic_Name once did not go to school for three days. During these three days, she organized her school essentials and cleaned up her room. Since she was working on a project before the break, she had time to finish it and she even had another project idea for her science class. She obtained a good grade on both projects. In fact, students who have taken breaks during long tests, like the SOL, say that after their break they had a better understanding of the test. Even the workforce workers are encouraged to take a few days off. It helps the worker get more creative. Even the owner of a business need a vacation. In fact, around 56% of entrepreneurs say that they came up with at least one new idea after a vacation. Inactivity helps prepare our minds for when we are active.

Scientist Albert Einstein once said, "Imagination is more important than knowledge." Now imagine yourself as a beginning engineer, sitting at your desk, aggravated because you can't come up with a new invention. All you have around you are textbooks but no image or thought of what your invention may be. If only you could imagine a new invention of some sort then maybe you could build something. But with no imagination, how can you build knowledge? I agree with Einstein's quote. I believe imagination is more important than knowledge.

I agree with Einstein's quote because having imagination is how we've had all our inventions yet. Without imagination how were many of the things we own invented? For example, the telephone. The telephone couldn't have been invented without someone imagining a device where you could communicate without leaving your home. You need imagination in order to make new things. Another example would be the camera. Whoever invented it, had to have imagination in order to think of a device that captures any moment almost in an instant. Even I, as a student, need imagination in order to make new things. For example, when making an essay, such as this one, I need to imagine of a good story hook that goes along with the prompt.

Furthermore, I believe in Einstein quote because without imagination, knowledge is almost useless. For example, when learning a new vocabulary list. You may know all the definitions but you can't put them in your own words or use the words in different instances. Why? Because you can't imagine it. You can't picture it, you just know the definitions. Another example is when reading a book. Knowing how to read isn't even near of what you need to fully comprehend a book. You need to imagine it. Picture the story in your mind in order to fully understand the book's theme, setting and tone.

Lastly, I agree in Einstein's quote because without imagination, all our decisions would be made carelessly. For instance, before you speak or move, most of the time you imagine what the outcome of that action will be. If not, the outcome won't be for the better. Another instance is when in an experiment, you hypothesize what the result of the experiment will be. That takes imagination. When signing a contract, it's needed to imagine the consequences of signing and not signing the contract. In other words, you need to imagine things before you decide to take them on. Knowledge isn't the only thing that will help you when making decisions.

In conclusion, Einstein's quote is correct in my perspective. Knowledge isn't the most important factor to have, imagination is key to everything you do and will do. You can't fully understand most things without imagining them. Can't go on inventing things before imagining them first. Also, you won't be able to make good decisions before imagining the outcome. All in all, imagination is also how you'll enjoy your life. Knowledge is great and all but it can't bring others as much happiness as imagination can. It's how we've been happy for all these years. Imagination is how we have gone so far in this world and how much we've survived.
